title.narrative: Strengthen access to integrated, quality curative health and nutrition services through early detection and treatment of SAM in Maiduguri and Jere LGA, Borno state

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis integrated project aims to reduce mortality and morbidity among internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities in crisis-affected areas of Jere Local Government Area (LGA) in Borno State, Nigeria. The intervention focuses on providing life-saving medical and nutritional assistance, particularly in areas where health risks are high due to ongoing conflict. Implemented by ALIMA, the project targets two main sectors: health and nutrition with the goal of improving access to essential community, primary, and secondary healthcare services, while also addressing severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and other nutritional needs, especially during peak periods and after. Support will be provided to three health centers (Muna, Shuwari, and Custom House) and two Inpatient Therapeutic Feeding Centers (UMTH and Maryam Abacha Hospital), reaching an estimated 69,601 direct beneficiaries . ltbrgtALIMA will offer free, quality nutritional and medical care to 8,991 children under five years old with uncomplicated SAM, and will ensure referral and care for an additional 1,958 children with medical complications. Beyond direct treatment, the project will strengthen the resilience of the health system through capacity building, community engagement, and preventive actions to combat malnutrition.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtEmphasis will be placed on cross-cutting themes including gender-based violence (GBV), protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), disability inclusion, gender mainstreaming, and accountability to affected populations (AAP). Special support will be provided to ensure that elderly and disabled individuals have access to care. Awareness-raising initiatives will help ensure the sustainability of outcomes, enabling communities to maintain health gains beyond the life of the project.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtOverall, ALIMA is seeking USD 322,743.97 for nutritional interventions and USD 145,000.91 for integrated health sector activities, aimed at scaling up, maintaining, and maximizing impact while ensuring the sustainability of operations.ltbrgtlt/pgt
